instruction: Exact row-level values or many columns matter most.
instructions: Table. Config: columns from Object.keys(data[0]); dataSource=data; rowKey index; pagination.
Polish: humanize headers (underscore->space); pagination true; no fake sorts unless asked; wrap in div.

REQUIRED: keep the conversionHints comment and replace dimension_column / measure_column with the real category and measure column names used in the result (xField=dimension, yField=measure). Example: // conversionHints: xField: 'Travel Type', yField: 'Travel Cost'.

REQUIRED when Excel format strings are provided: build a columnFormats map { columnOrMeasureName: formatString } for matching fields only, and add column.render that applies the Excel pattern (e.g. toFixed for 0.00 / 0.0#, or leave string as-is if not numeric). Example: render: (value) => { const fmt = columnFormats[key]; if (fmt && value != null && value !== '' && !isNaN(Number(value))) { if (fmt === '0.00') return Number(value).toFixed(2); if (fmt === '0.0') return Number(value).toFixed(1); if (fmt.includes('#,##0')) return Number(value).toLocaleString(undefined, { minimumFractionDigits: (fmt.split('.')[1] || '').replace(/[^0]/g, '').length, maximumFractionDigits: (fmt.split('.')[1] || '').replace(/[^0]/g, '').length }); return String(value); } return value; }. Do not invent formats for unmatched columns.
